review_headline: Back to 1 star – Seven-day "escalation" results in another excuse not to honour the warranty
review_body:
I originally gave AliExpress 1 star, increased it to 2 stars because they appeared to finally be paying attention to my complaint, and gave them the benefit of the doubt.

I now regret doing that.

After AliExpress told me that my case had been escalated, I waited SEVEN DAYS for them to deal with it.

After all that time, I received this response:

"As you did not raise any dispute, we are unable to support your refund request."

That is the latest excuse.

And it is particularly infuriating because it comes after weeks of AliExpress repeatedly asking me for evidence.

Let's recap what has actually happened.

I purchased an IPL device on 1 December 2025.

It worked normally for approximately eight months and then failed. It still powers on and the modes can be selected, but it produces no IPL flashes whatsoever.

The manufacturer's manual states a 12-month warranty.

I contacted the seller.

The seller repeatedly told me they would resolve the problem and contact me.

They didn't.

I contacted AliExpress.

AliExpress repeatedly asked me for photographs, a description and video evidence.

I provided them. Multiple times.

They then told me the case had been escalated.

I waited seven days.

And now they have suddenly decided that because I "did not raise any dispute", they cannot support my refund request.

Seriously?

If this was always going to be the reason for refusing the claim, why did AliExpress repeatedly ask me for videos and other evidence?

Why did they allow me to repeatedly provide that evidence?

Why did they escalate the case?

Why did nobody tell me at the beginning that they would refuse to consider the matter on this basis?

And most importantly:

Why has nobody actually addressed the 12-month warranty?

This is what makes the whole experience so incredibly frustrating.

Every time I answer one of their requirements, another obstacle appears.

First it was:

"Your order is over six months old. Provide evidence."

I provided the evidence.

Then they asked for the video again.

I provided a new video.

Then they said the case had been escalated.

I waited seven days.

Now it is:

"You did not raise a dispute."

At no point have they actually addressed the fundamental issue:

A product with a stated 12-month warranty failed after approximately eight months, and I have provided clear evidence of the fault.

Instead of dealing with that warranty claim, I appear to be going around in circles while AliExpress finds another procedural reason not to deal with it.

I have been patient. I have cooperated. I have supplied the evidence they requested. I have waited through their escalations.

My patience has now run out.

I am returning this review to 1 star.

This is not what I consider customer service.

I will continue to document this case and update this review if AliExpress finally decides to properly address the warranty claim.

AliExpress: I am not asking you for special treatment. I am asking you to explain why a product that failed within its stated 12-month warranty is apparently not being covered — and to stop moving the goalposts every time I satisfy your latest request.

ALI has no credibility and is unethical. I tried again because some of the products are unique but this is the last time I get burnt

I gave each agent the order ID and a screen of the guarantee from the orders. Why they would need more than a item description and order ID is beyond me.  

Everytime something is delivered late, which is 90% of the time, I have to fight for a lousy dollar. 

Im done with Ali, im just returning the products and items that are still being delivered. It's not worth waiting over 2 weeks for an order and then the drama and stress to have to fight with Ali to get them to honor their guarantee.

The prompt told me to cancel my return request and then add both items to a new return. Problem started now, being unable to cancel, it then said to contact customer support. Which I did, the Agent (person not AI) said that the ALSO could not cancel my request, and gave no reason why. They insisted on me sending both back and sticking both labels on the return. This seemed impossible to me & I mentioned that Aus post would not process that package with 2 return labels. They said this would be forwarded to a 'specialist' team to make sure my items arrived and to confirm that X2 returns were inside the origional box. They advised I take a video of me boxing 2 glasses into the origional box in case of verification at a later stage.
Next day I posted the items, Aus post would only allow 1 label (as I assumed and flagged as a problem) once I got home I started another Agent chat to confirm the situation I was in was understood and that this would be sent to whoever is 'inspecting'the items on arrival. Upon inspection they will see, X2 items and be able to process the second return. 
This Agent understood my issue and also flagged a 'specialist'team to contact me. 

The specialist team requested video /photo evidence of the boxing, which I sent, also a weight of the item, which Aus post never did (nor was I told to on my end) The conversation feeds with all agents disappears after the 'end chat' so other than a couple of screenshots I was unable to 'prove'what they said to me.
Currently I now have no glassware and they have denied me a refund. This was the response from the specialist team, insufficient evidence. The warehouse has literal proof of the items in their possession. How that is not evidence is beyond me. Hollow sympathy with zero willingness to help me. I followed their instructions and now have no product and no money. This is stealing. 
The inspection would clearly show a discrepancy in the return item, having more than the item under the return. Either they do not inspect items, or they are hiding behind beurocratic tape to willingly screw their customers. Disgraceful experience & complete waste of time trying to get them to do the right thing.

review_headline: AliExpress refuses to refund me even after receiving the returned item
review_body:
Order number: 1121706383388373

The item arrived with poor build quality and defective, misaligned drawers, so I opened a dispute.

AliExpress instructed me to return the product to an address in Bremen, Germany. Because the parcel was around 30 kg, normal postal return services could not handle it. I repeatedly asked AliExpress for a proper return label or practical solution, but all I received were generic and automated replies.

I eventually arranged the return myself through Eurosender/UPS and paid EUR 146.95 for shipping. AliExpress had also told me that the return shipping cost would be reimbursed.

The return was delayed because UPS needed a German contact number. I contacted AliExpress multiple times asking for help, but again received no useful assistance. AliExpress then closed the dispute while the parcel was still in transit.

The package was ultimately successfully delivered in Bremen on 25 August, and UPS provided proof of delivery. I sent AliExpress the shipping label and proof of delivery, exactly the type of evidence they had previously requested.

Despite this, AliExpress has now explicitly refused to return my money, without giving any proper reason.

So the situation is simple: the seller has the returned cabinet, AliExpress refuses to refund my DKK 1,863.18, and I am also still owed the EUR 146.95 return shipping cost.

The worst part is the customer service. No matter how much evidence I provide, I mostly receive automated replies that do not address the actual issue.

I would strongly advise against buying expensive or bulky items from AliExpress. If something goes wrong, you may return the product successfully and still have AliExpress refuse to give your money back.

Update: AliExpress has now refunded the DKK 1,863.18 purchase price for the cabinet, so that part of the complaint has finally been resolved.

However, the issue is not fully resolved yet.

I paid EUR 146.95 to return the defective cabinet through Eurosender/UPS because the parcel was around 30 kg and the normal return options were not suitable. AliExpress had previously confirmed that the return shipping cost would also be reimbursed.

So I appreciate that the cabinet refund has now been processed, but I am still waiting for reimbursement of the EUR 146.95 return shipping cost.

I will update this review again once the remaining amount has been refunded.

review_headline: Quick to take money and worst for solving issues.
review_body:
Bought two items from AliExpress. One arrived within a week, was exactly as described, and the shipping was very fast. The other showed the same estimated delivery date but ended up arriving three weeks later.

By that point, I needed the item urgently, so I had already bought another one locally. I then tried to return the AliExpress item, and that’s where the real headache started.

The entire returns process seems deliberately complicated. Half the time, the system doesn’t work properly, and you have to jump through hoops just to get the return accepted. Eventually, I managed to send it back to the vague address they provided, but the address doesn’t even appear to be recognised on the courier’s tracking system.

I submitted all the required information and proof, only to be told they can’t find the return.

Honestly, save yourself the time and hassle. If something goes wrong, the returns process is an absolute nightmare. Avoid AliExpress like the plague.

review_headline: AliExpress – Service zur Vermeidung von Lösungen (Kundenservice)
review_body:
Der AliExpress-Kundenservice scheint nicht darauf ausgerichtet zu sein, Probleme zu lösen, sondern vielmehr darauf, sie so kompliziert und ermüdend zu machen, dass Kunden irgendwann aufgeben.

Der Verkäufer hat schriftlich bestätigt, dass zwischen dem von mir bestellten und dem tatsächlich gelieferten Produkt eine Abweichung besteht, und dies als „Fabrik-Druckfehler“ erklärt. Trotzdem verlangt AliExpress weiterhin ein Unboxing-Video, obwohl ich vor der Lieferung niemals darüber informiert wurde, dass ein solches Video erforderlich ist.

Damit nicht genug: Nun verlangt AliExpress zusätzlich, dass ich das Produkt professionell oder in einem Labor auf das verwendete Material testen lasse. Dies, obwohl der Verkäufer bereits schriftliche Erklärungen zum Produkt abgegeben hat und die wesentlichen Punkte meines Streits dokumentiert sind.

Ständig neue, möglicherweise kostenpflichtige oder zuvor nicht angekündigte Nachweise zu verlangen, wirkt nicht wie der Versuch, ein Kundenproblem zu lösen. Es vermittelt vielmehr den Eindruck, dass der Kunde so lange belastet und ermüdet werden soll, bis er schließlich aufgibt.

Nun bin auch ich müde und habe genug davon.

Ein Kunde sollte nicht einen derart komplizierten und frustrierenden Prozess durchlaufen müssen, nur damit eine nachvollziehbar dokumentierte Reklamation überhaupt sachlich geprüft wird.

Diese Erfahrung hat mein Vertrauen in AliExpress vollständig zerstört. Ich werde nie wieder bei AliExpress einkaufen und werde auch andere Menschen über diese Erfahrung informieren, bevor sie sich für einen Kauf auf dieser Plattform entscheiden.

review_headline: Practical Tool 47 Store: Lying about his stock
review_body:
Shortly after placing my  order to the store called "Practical Tool 47 Store" (ID:912216240) on the AliExpress platform, I received a cryptic message from the store keepers offering me to send another version of the product I ordered, a cheaper, less features, but it was hard to understand, they also did not propose a compensation for the price difference.
Ordered: ESP32-S3-RS485-CAN-U
What I believe they meant: a clone of the ESP32-S3-RS485-CAN.

Msg: "Dear customer, do you mind if we switch to another product to ship to you? The functions are the same but the antenna installation method is different. Looking forward to your reply~"

It took them three full days to kind of answer in the meanwhile I was annoyed by their AI chatbot.
The answer was again unclear, and looking more and more like a scram.
I contacted AliExpress CS to discuss the situation, a case was escalated, the answer: this time we will take note of your comment... not much from that side.

At the time of writing this review the Store change the product labels and remove the genuine Waveshare reference for "onboad/external antenna"... this is most likely a clone but at the same price (even more expensive compared to the official Waveshare store, which unfortunately cannot ship easily to my address)...

After 8 days the Store cancelled my order, without my consent, without consulting me first, a refund is one the way from AliExpress, hopefully it will reach me in the coming days, but with the 2% extra fees from my bank I lost about 4% of the invoice amount... this is annoying to say the least.

The worse might be the last message from the Store:
"It doesn't matter, we have finished stocking, we will still order it according to your order, thank you~
Dear Customer, We have accepted your refund request. Pls check your account later. The refund will transfer to your account soon. Have a nice day! Best regards"

Again: I never asked for a refund, but to have my initial order fulfilled professionally.
I let you judge.

review_headline: Alléchée par un prix défiant toute…
review_body:
Alléchée par un prix défiant toute concurrence je suis retournée sur la plateforme d'Aliexpress que je ne fréquentais plus depuis longtemps. Suite à cet achat j' ai constaté que l'adresse d'expédition était une adresse périmée. Ils ne m'ont pas laissé de choix non plus au moment de l'achat et ont choisi cette adresse de manière arbitraire! Je ne l'ai vue qu'une fois l'achat fait. J' ai essayé de changer l'adresse immédiatement, le link n' a pas fonctionné. Ensuite, j' ai essayé d'annuler la vente, le link n' a pas fonctionné. J' ai donc contacté le service client et un agent m'a certifié qu'il procédait à l' annulation et que tout était bien annulé mais que cela prendrait 24h à être affiché. Peu avant minuit, un mail m'annonçant que les articles avaient été expédiés me met en alerte. Comment est ce possible ? Je recontacte le service client qui me répète en boucle que l'on ne peut rien faire car les produits ont été expédiés. J' explique que c'est entièrement de leur faute puisque un agent m'a assuré que la vente était annulée et que j' ai lâché l'affaire à ce moment-là faisant entièrement confiance à Aliexpress ! On m'a tout simplement menti pour que je cesse d'insister sur l'annulation de cette commande! Je ne travaille plus à cette adresse depuis deux ans, c'est un lieu public donc très gênant pour moi que l'on expédie à cette adresse. Il n' y a rien à faire, robots et agents humains répètent en boucle qu'une fois que la réception aura eu lieu, je serai remboursée. Autant expliquer la situation à un mur... Ils ont été incapables d'annuler la commande et m'ont menti au sujet de l'annulation, et refusent de rembourser avant la non livraison qui aura lieu dans un endroit public où les paquets sont déposés dans une boîte collective au nom de cet établissement (et non du mien) et qui apparaîtra comme livré alors que je ne peux le retirer puisque je n' y suis plus et que j' ai quitté la région. Une chose est sûre, cela me servira de leçon pour supprimer définitivement mon compte mais je ne lâcherai pas prise avant d'avoir eu raison de cause! 
"Nouvelle" réponse d'Aliexpress, zéro solution, ils répètent en boucle la même chose: ils tournent leurs clients en bourrique !
Évidemment ils répondent par mail et non pas dans la suite de ce message car ce serait bête de montrer sa mauvaise foi ici, voici donc leur mail de "nouvelle" réponse et "solution de conflit":
Cher client,

Nous vous remercions de nous avoir signalé ce problème. Veuillez accepter nos plus sincères excuses pour la gêne occasionnée.

Concernant la commande n° 3075800106286240, suite à votre demande, nous vous confirmons que le vendeur a déjà expédié votre colis, actuellement en transit. Nous regrettons de vous informer qu'il n'est plus possible de modifier l'adresse de livraison. Toutefois, nous vous proposons les options suivantes :

1. Contacter le transporteur : Dès l'arrivée du colis dans votre ville, vous pourrez contacter le transporteur afin de demander une livraison à une nouvelle adresse.
2. Refuser la livraison : Si nécessaire, vous pouvez refuser le colis. Veuillez noter cependant que le refus de livraison peut entraîner une déduction des frais de port pour le remboursement. Nous vous remercions de votre compréhension.

Nous vous remercions de votre compréhension. Si vous rencontrez d'autres problèmes lors de votre achat, n'hésitez pas à nous contacter par e-mail.

Cordialement,
L'équipe du service client AliExpress

Ça fait trois jours que je reçois en boucle ce genre de réponse et chaque fois malgré les réclamations même réponse...tiens donc ils ne savaient pas que le colis serait refusé et non livré ? Ils ont été avertis immédiatement après l'achat et n'ont rien fait, maintenant ils refusent de rembourser alors qu'ils avaient promis que dès que le colis serait remboursé, ils le feraient. review_headline: Il a fallu engager un véritable combat pour être remboursé (360 euros)
review_body:
Je mets à jour mon avis pour préciser qu’AliExpress a finalement procédé au remboursement intégral de mes 359,04 €. Mais il aura fallu des semaines de démarches totalement disproportionnées pour obtenir le remboursement d’une commande que je n’avais jamais reçue.

Le suivi GLS comportait des informations incohérentes, indiquant notamment une livraison à Aulnay-sous-Bois, alors que le colis devait m’être remis dans un point relais du 20e arrondissement de Paris. Le point relais m’a confirmé n’avoir aucune trace du colis.

Malgré les très nombreux justificatifs fournis, AliExpress m’a renvoyé encore et encore vers GLS, en exigeant un document officiel de non-livraison. Or GLS m’a confirmé par écrit qu’il ne pouvait pas me fournir ce document et que c’était à l’expéditeur de les contacter directement.

J’étais donc enfermé dans une boucle absurde : AliExpress exigeait un document de GLS pour me rembourser, tandis que GLS expliquait que ce document devait être demandé par l’expéditeur.

Le vendeur Marketplace, Anbernic Europe Local Store, m’a ensuite proposé de m’expédier un nouvel exemplaire, reconnaissant ainsi qu'il existait bien un problème avec le premier envoi, mais sans accepter pour autant de me rembourser.

Le plus incroyable concerne le service client AliExpress lui-même. Une première fois, un conseiller m’a affirmé explicitement par messagerie qu’un remboursement intégral de 359,04 € avait été accordé et serait effectué sous 24 heures. C'était faux : aucun remboursement n'a suivi et je n'ai reçu aucun e-mail officiel de confirmation. Lorsque j'ai recontacté AliExpress, d'autres conseillers m'ont indiqué qu'ils n'avaient aucune trace de cet accord de remboursement ! J'ai alors été une nouvelle fois renvoyé vers GLS et sommé de produire le même document impossible à obtenir.

Il a donc fallu recommencer les démarches et obtenir une nouvelle escalade du dossier avant qu'AliExpress finisse réellement par valider puis effectuer le remboursement.

Entre-temps, j’avais dû multiplier les réclamations, fournir une attestation de non-réception, documenter l'absence du colis au point relais, effectuer un signalement SignalConso, déposer une plainte auprès de la police et envoyer une mise en demeure en recommandé avec l'ensemble du dossier (ce qui, soit dit en passant, m'a coûté environ 20 euros que je ne récupèrerai pas...).

Je reconnais donc qu’AliExpress m’a finalement remboursé les 359,04 € et je mets mon témoignage à jour pour le préciser.

Mais le remboursement final ne peut pas effacer la manière dont ce litige a été géré : semaines de démarches, réponses standardisées en boucle, services qui se contredisent, exigence répétée d’un document que le transporteur refuse de remettre au destinataire, et même annonce d’un remboursement sous 24 h qui n’existait manifestement pas dans leur système.

Le problème n'est finalement pas seulement qu'un colis puisse se perdre — cela peut arriver à n'importe quel commerçant. Le véritable problème est ce qui se passe chez AliExpress lorsque quelque chose tourne mal.

Après cette expérience, je ne commanderai plus jamais de produit de valeur sur AliExpress.

⭐ 1/5 malgré le remboursement final, en raison d’une gestion du litige que je considère absolument catastrophique.

review_headline: I strongly warn against ordering from…
review_body: I strongly warn against ordering from UKing Overseas Local Store and AliExpress. Despite returning the items, I only received a small partial refund. After four weeks, they are now claiming that I did not return the order in full. I believe this is a complete scam.

Poor-quality products, very slow delivery, inconvenient returns

1. Poor-quality products

I purchased nine products from AliExpress. Two of them,a miniature frying pan and a miniature knife, were so small and impractical that they looked more like children’s toy cookware than functional kitchen tools. Although the listings presented them as cookware suitable for frying eggs and preparing food, neither product was suitable for normal kitchen use. When my wife saw them, she could not help laughing because they looked like toys.

2. Very slow delivery

The delivery problems were widespread rather than isolated. One order took 14 days to arrive. Another took 16 days, with no tracking update for nearly seven days after August 20; I received a response only after I complained. Another shipment was marked as undeliverable because of "no access" but there was no known access problem at my address, and I received no notification or other indication that a delivery attempt had been made. I asked AliExpress to investigate what had happened, but no meaningful investigation or explanation was provided.

Most significantly, after purchasing only nine products, I received eight separate $1 coupons explicitly marked “Issued for late delivery.” AliExpress’s own records therefore confirm how frequently my purchases were delivered late.

3. Inconvenient returns

When I requested a return for the miniature frying pan, I submitted a photograph that clearly showed its extremely small, toy-like appearance. AliExpress nevertheless demanded extensive additional evidence, including a video of the packaging and product, close-ups of defects, a functional test, and records of communication with the seller.

Both the frying pan and the knife were unsuitable for normal use, but the return system appeared to allow only one product from the order to be returned. I may therefore be forced to keep and pay for another unusable item.

The $1 late-delivery coupons are also of little practical value because only one can be used per order. Using all eight would require me to place multiple additional orders and spend more money on AliExpress. These restrictions make both the return process and the supposed compensation unnecessarily inconvenient.

Update: AliExpress states in its public reply that it emailed me a “final solution.” However, the email I received did not resolve my complaint. It requested evidence again and stated that the seller would cover return shipping if the items did not match the listed dimensions.

I have already acknowledged that dimensions were listed. My complaint concerns product images that made the very small frying pan and knife appear much larger. I still have not received a clear answer on whether both items can be returned for a full refund with prepaid return shipping.

Sending an email is not the same as providing a resolution. My complaint remains unresolved.

Some of the items I ordered were broken or missing.....both out of the manufacture package and out of the shipping bag because AliExpress did NOT properly seal the shipping bag and two of the bag I received had a large opening at the top because they only taped the top part of the bag and not the underneath part of the bag.  Also, some of the items I ordered were substituted without asking and they were substituted with a lesser quality.  (I had ordered some 925 sterling charms...which were more expensive...and they send plain round cheap charms.  AliExpress refused to give a replacement or a refund - totaled over $300.00 for all of the problems.  They gave me the runaround for months.  Absolutely horrible.  Since then, several other people have told me they experienced the same thing.....broken items, not receiving what they ordered, packages being delivered to someone else's house as evidenced by photos and AliExpress would not issued a replacement or refund for them either.  Clearly when you have this many negative reviews, it's only a matter of time to find out for yourself.

Très mauvaise expérience – produit non conforme et service client décevant

J’ai commandé un kit de conversion pour vélo électrique clairement présenté comme « With 48V 18AH Battery », pour lequel j’ai payé 568,56 €. Or, j’ai reçu le kit sans la batterie, alors que le modèle livré coûte plus de 300 € de moins que celui que j’avais commandé et payé.

J’ai contacté le vendeur à plusieurs reprises afin qu’il m’envoie la batterie prévue dans ma commande. Malgré mes demandes, il a refusé de trouver une solution au problème.

J’ai donc ouvert un litige auprès d’AliExpress et fourni tous les éléments permettant de démontrer clairement la différence entre le produit commandé et celui qui m’avait été livré.

À ma grande surprise, AliExpress a rejeté ma demande sans fournir d’explication concrète et satisfaisante, alors que les preuves étaient pourtant parfaitement claires. AliExpress ne m’a accordé qu’un remboursement partiel de 85,28 €, alors que le produit reçu ne correspondait manifestement pas à celui que j’avais acheté.

J’ai finalement dû faire appel à PayPal. Après avoir examiné mon dossier et les preuves fournies, PayPal a accepté ma réclamation et m’a remboursé la somme restante. J’ai ainsi pu récupérer la totalité des 568,56 € que j’avais initialement payés.

Je suis extrêmement déçu, aussi bien par le vendeur que par la manière dont AliExpress a géré mon litige. Je m’attendais à un service client plus sérieux et, surtout, à une véritable protection du client lorsqu’un problème de conformité est aussi clairement documenté.

Je ne recommande absolument pas ce vendeur et, après cette expérience, je n’achèterai plus sur AliExpress.

Si vous décidez malgré tout d’acheter sur AliExpress, je vous conseille vivement de payer avec PayPal. Dans mon cas, c’est finalement PayPal qui m’a apporté la protection que je n’ai pas obtenue auprès d’AliExpress. Sans PayPal, je serais probablement resté avec un produit qui ne correspondait pas à ma commande et avec une perte financière importante.

Very disappointing experience – product not as described and extremely poor customer support

I ordered an electric bicycle conversion kit that was clearly advertised as “With 48V 18AH Battery” and paid €568.56. However, I received the kit without the battery, even though the version I received costs more than €300 less than the one I had ordered and paid for.
I contacted the seller several times and gave them every opportunity to correct the mistake by sending the battery included in my order. Unfortunately, the seller refused to resolve the problem.

I then opened a dispute with AliExpress and provided clear evidence showing the difference between what I had ordered and what I had actually received.
What happened next was extremely disappointing. AliExpress rejected my claim without providing any meaningful or convincing explanation, despite the evidence being clear. I was granted only a partial refund of €85.28, leaving me significantly out of pocket for a product that was not the one I had purchased.
I eventually had to turn to PayPal. After reviewing my case and the evidence, PayPal accepted my claim and refunded the outstanding amount, allowing me to finally recover the full €568.56 I had originally paid.
This experience has completely destroyed my confidence in AliExpress. I am particularly disappointed by the lack of customer protection and by the way my dispute was handled. When a customer receives a product that is clearly different from the one ordered and has documented evidence to prove it, I believe the platform should protect the customer rather than leave them to resolve the problem themselves.
I do not recommend this seller, and after this experience I will no longer purchase from AliExpress.
If you nevertheless decide to buy from AliExpress, I strongly recommend using PayPal as your payment method. In my case, PayPal provided the customer protection that I did not receive from AliExpress.

review_headline: Why You Can No Longer Trust AliExpress Ratings! Bought a 97€ Dashcam on Ali, Got a Brick and a 19€ Refund!
review_body:
Why You Can No Longer Trust AliExpress Ratings! Bought a 97€ Dashcam on Ali, Got a Brick and a 19€ Refund! Hello everyone. I want to share a story about how AliExpress artificially maintains high ratings for scam sellers by depriving buyers of the opportunity to write the truth, and how their "arbitration" system works strictly in the seller's favor.  I bought a dashboard camera for my car, and it turned out to be completely defective. The GPS signal drops constantly, and the time zone resets all the time. The store sent me a firmware update, but it fails to install—the process gets interrupted, the dashcam reboots, and this loop keeps happening over and over, along with other issues regarding coordinates and software stability. I paid 97 euros for this device! While I was trying to figure out these issues with the store (which took about a month, if not more), I opened a dispute and requested a partial refund of 30 euros. AliExpress, however, decided that 19.44 euros would be more than enough for me, claiming that I was asking for too much money relative to these problems. The seller barely participated in the dispute; they rejected it only once, asking me to send data from the dashcam, which I did. After that, they took no further action and didn't contest anything else.I appealed the decision, but AliExpress stood its ground. They rushed to transfer the 19.44 euros almost on the exact same day, seemingly just to argue later that the money had already been refunded and nothing more could be done. That is exactly what happened, and those were the exact replies I received. Later on, the seller even confirmed that I was not to blame for the defects, acknowledged that I had received a partial refund, and offered me a 5-euro discount as compensation. For some reason, the refund amount shown on the seller's side was completely different—21.67 euros. The real catch happened when I wanted to leave a review after finishing all my testing and discussions with the seller. It turned out that the window of time to leave feedback is strictly limited. In my opinion, this is done intentionally so that people leave positive reviews before they even have a chance to properly test the product, preventing them from leaving an honest, negative one later. As a result, looking at all those filtered positive reviews, AliExpress's reputation remains untarnished. As I mentioned in another post, they encourage scammers by protecting them instead of fighting them. I have attached the screenshots regarding this case, some of which are in Russian.

review_headline: Update to: I ordered an item on AliExpress and it was never delivered
review_body:
I ordered an item on AliExpress, and the seller chose DPD as the courier for delivery. As most people in Europe know, that’s a bad idea to begin with, but I didn't have a choice in the matter. As ussual, DPD didn't deliver the package to my home and they even showed up at the drop-off point after closing time. DPD's "customer service" actually confirmed this. DPD then simply decided to return the item. This is clearly visible in the tracking details. I filed a complaint with AliExpress and submitted the tracking info as evidence, but the complaint was rejected due to a lack of proof. How else are you supposed to prove you didn't receive something? A photo of your empty hands? No more AliExpress thieves for me. TEMU is far more customer-oriented.

Update 28/08/2026:

After Writing the above review I was contacted again by AliExpress apologizing and informing me the purchase was refunded.  I do appreciate that.  However, I regret having to spend time writing a bad review in frustration, when this solution could have been given immediately.  I did not give any extra information additionally to when I first made the complaint.  Giving proof of not receiving the item should be enough for a refund, instead it is only given after writing a bad review.  AliExpress definitely still needs to work on their customer service!

NUOVO AGGIORNAMENTO – Comunicazioni contraddittorie da AliExpress

Dopo aver inviato una formale diffida per il mancato rimborso di €105,69, ho ricevuto da AliExpress due comunicazioni completamente contraddittorie a distanza di pochi minuti.

Nella prima email mi viene comunicato che la mia richiesta è “in handling”, associata al work order n. 2053808660944605, e che devo attendere la risposta del relativo reparto.

Pochi minuti dopo ricevo invece una seconda comunicazione nella quale AliExpress afferma che non può approvare il rimborso, sostenendo che il prodotto restituito sarebbe diverso da quello acquistato.

La seconda risposta appare inoltre fortemente automatizzata e generata da un sistema AI, con una formulazione estremamente generica e senza alcuna risposta concreta alle contestazioni giuridiche e alle richieste specifiche contenute nella mia diffida.

Quindi quale sarebbe la posizione ufficiale di AliExpress? La mia pratica è ancora in gestione oppure è stata definitivamente respinta?

Continuano inoltre a basarsi sulle fotografie del magazzino, che non dimostrano che l’articolo fotografato fosse effettivamente contenuto nel pacco da me consegnato. Il tracking InPost dimostra invece che il pacco del reso è stato regolarmente consegnato.

Ho chiesto di verificare la situazione con InPost e di acquisire le evidenze oggettive della spedizione, in particolare i pesi registrati alla presa in carico e alla consegna, ma non ho ricevuto tali verifiche.

Mi aspetto quindi una risposta coerente, concreta e specificamente riferita alla mia contestazione, non comunicazioni automatiche contraddittorie.

I purchased an Executive Chair for an agreed Total = AU$757.91.  (AU$376.69 and an additional AU$312.32 for Shipping Costs. Tax  at AU$68.90)  The amount came out of my PayPal Account. For over a week the Seller wanted an additional AU$260.00 for shipping, whilst holding onto my money I already paid. I raised a concern with AliExpress. It was such a waste of time with AliExpress with the final statement from them stating Following an internal review of the information provided, we regret to inform you that the report has been deemed unsubstantiated. The reason for this decision is as follows:
The reported item/content does not violate platform regulations. The refunded my money in the end.

I cannot understand why AliExpress states that: "The reported item/content does not violate platform regulations" This response is quite concerning, and I do not understand why the ticket has been closed.

My primary concern is what prevents sellers from advertising products with a stated shipping fee, collecting payment from buyers, and then later claiming that additional shipping costs are required. Sellers should be responsible for maintaining accurate and up-to-date shipping charges before listing their products for sale. Buyers should not be placed in a position where they are forced to either pay more after the transaction or wait for a refund.

In this situation, the seller holds the buyer's funds while the matter is being disputed, potentially benefiting from access to that money during the process. Meanwhile, the buyer loses the opportunity to earn interest or otherwise use those funds. The seller can simply issue a refund at a later date without bearing any responsibility for the inconvenience, delay, or financial impact caused.

This does not seem fair or consistent with good business practices. It also raises concerns about making larger purchases through AliExpress in the future if the same issue can occur without consequence.

I believe sellers should be held accountable for providing accurate shipping costs and that buyers should receive compensation when errors arise due to the seller's failure to keep their shipping information current. In my view, the seller should bear the responsibility for this mistake, not the buyer.

review_headline: This has turned into a giant scam
review_body:
This has turned into a giant scam. Do not buy anything expensive or important here.

As many other people say, you will end up with defective products.

When you complain about something that is not a visual defect, AliExpress declines the claim with the statement "We have carefully revisited all
the proof provided, including the newly updated proof and found that the proof is not effective enough to prove your claim."

There is no way of replying to these decisions, you have to start from an AI chat every time and fight your way to a frist line agent, then an appeal agent, which might be replying on email after up to a few months. 

From the time of their message, months later, you have exactly 24h until the case gets closed and you can no longer reply to the email. Then you start the process over.

I'm giving up now, to get my money back, and on AliExpress in general. This happened to me a few times on cheaper items, where I just ignored the loss. But this is the tipping point - there is no trust left.

Spend your money elsewhere! They protect the sellers and let them get away with shipping defect products. This also gets evident after you shop elsewhere. 75% of my last order on AliExpress was defective compared to a few percent on the other app I use.

There are other Chinese apps with magnitudes of better services and buyer protection. 

In other apps, you simply get free returns, on time per order. Simply return it if you don't like it. If it is clearly broken, others won't even ask you to return the product, just issue a refund.

Read other reviews, you will find the same story. Use another app and don't lose your money.

J’ai commandé un bac à pizza avec couvercle hermétique le 16 juillet 2026.
Le bac est arrivé comme prévu avec le couvercle, sauf qu’il n’est pas hermétique. Le couvercle est plus petit et se balade au niveau du haut du bac.
J’ai ouvert un litige auprès du service client et ce dernier m’a dit de voir avec le vendeur.
Le vendeur m’a proposé un remboursement partiel de 8$, puis après négociation, m’a proposé 10$.
Le vendeur m’a demandé de clôturer le litige pour procéder au remboursement. 
J’ai donc repris contact avec le service client et ce dernier m’a dit de ne pas clôturer le litige et qu’il s’en occupait.
Après plusieurs jours, et j’ai repris contact avec le service client, puisque je n’avais plus de nouvelles.
Ils m’ont demandé de transmettre les échanges de messages entre le vendeur et moi pour prouver l’accord. Le litige a traîné pendant plus d’un mois et après avoir eu plus de 15 interlocuteurs, j’ai pris contact par téléphone avec AliExpress où un agent m’a dit de clôturer le litige et d’en refaire un pour renvoyer le bac. 
J’ai donc clôturé et refais un nouveau litige pour avoir une nouvelle étiquette de retour, sauf que l’application AliExpress a planté et m’a fait un remboursement partiel.
J’ai passé des appels au service client et contacté par messages également, mais ils n’ont pas résolu le problème.
Le vendeur est un escroc, car après la clôture du litige, il n’a pas voulu honorer sa parole sur le remboursement des 10$ et le service client m’a induit en erreur et m’a menti à plusieurs reprises.
Ce site est une arnaque monumentale avec des vendeurs qui sont des escrocs et un service client malhonnête.
Je ne recommande pas du tout ce site chinois qui est malveillant.

Suite de ce dossier :

Le service client de AliExpress envoi des mails contradictoires et complètement malhonnête.
Il continu sur la même ligne, en disant qu’ils vont m’aider, qu’ils sont là pour régler le litige et envoie des mails pour dire qu’ils peuvent rembourser partiellement de 2€ et quelques centimes, puis d’autres mails ils disent qu’ils ne peuvent pas rembourser partiellement et quelques centimes si je veux renvoyer le bac, il faut que le vendeur soit d’accord. Or, le vendeur est un escroc notoire qui ne donne pas son aval pour le renvoi, les commentaires sur sa page parlent d’eux-mêmes, à savoir très négatifs. 
AliExpress continu d’être malhonnête dans ses démarches et je ne recommande pas du tout d’aller sur cette plateforme qui ne règle pas les litiges.

review_headline: DO NOT PURCHASE ANYTHING OF ALIEXPRESS
review_body:
If you are trying to buy anything off AliExpress, especially high value items, stop! The listings claiming the item are "In Stock" are almost entirely phantom inventory.

99% of the time these sellers do not actually have the physical item sitting in a warehouse. Instead, they operate as middlemen. They list it as available to boost their store’s search visibility. When you spend your money, they scramble to source it locally in China.

When they inevitably fail because the item is unavailable, they will message you asking you to cancel the order.

They do this because if they cancel it themselves, AliExpress severely penalizes their store. By making you cancel, they keep their seller metrics perfect while your money (in my case of dollars) is locked up for days in refund processing.

Save yourself the headache and frozen funds. Purchase through authorized, dedicated collectible retailers with transparent waitlists instead.

I ordered a Junsun 10" Android car radio (order #3073416525752010) which never arrived. AliExpress itself confirmed the refund and even shows a "Refund processed and submitted to the financial institution" status but the refund then shows as "Refund failed."

Since then I have been stuck in an endless loop with AliExpress customer service for months:

I have received the exact same automated email over 15 times, asking me to submit my bank details via the same link.
I have submitted my bank details more than 10 times, through the requested form, and directly in chat.
Every single chat agent (I've spoken to at least 8 different agents/bots under names like Abdelhamid, Dan, Vyn, Youmna, Mohamed) gives the identical scripted response: apologizing, asking for the same bank details again, and promising escalation to a "senior team" or "higher management."
I was told multiple times that my case was "escalated" and that I would hear back within 48 hours, then within 1-3 working days. Each time, the follow-up was the same template message asking for bank details all over again proving no one had actually reviewed my case.
A "senior team response" was logged in the system, which turned out to be the same copy-pasted request for bank information.
I was also, without my consent, nudged toward accepting the refund as a "coupon" via a "Fast Refund (Bonus)" option instead of the cash refund via bank transfer that I originally requested and confirmed.
A chargeback was apparently initiated on their end (2026-08-07) which I have never received clear written confirmation about.

I have a Klarna reference and a Case ID (2053808611884772) and a complete chat history documenting this entire pattern.

This is not a one-off mistake  it is a repeated, systemic pattern of stalling customers with scripted responses instead of resolving valid, confirmed refunds. €79.28 may not sound like much, but the way this has been handled  the same non-answer over and over for months  is completely unacceptable for a company of this size.

I would strongly caution anyone dealing with AliExpress customer service on a refund issue: document everything, because you will likely need it to escalate outside their own chat system (Klarna, consumer protection authorities, etc.), as their internal escalation process appears to not actually function.

review_body: We received a demaged item from the seller and they will not repair and change

Refund Dispute – Order 8213871674453110

I am disputing the decision regarding order 8213871674453110, a 28-inch human hair wig that cost approximately $80. The wig arrived severely cut, with uneven lengths throughout and only one very small section reaching the advertised length. It was also poorly constructed, badly uneven, and had much lower density than advertised, making it completely unusable.
The item is advertised as a 28-inch product with a 200% density, which should weigh over 300 grams. However, after weighing the product myself, it only registers 180 grams. This is a severe shortage in weight and density compared to what was promised.
I submitted videos and extensive evidence clearly showing these defects and that the product was not as advertised. Despite this, the decision favored the seller, and I was offered only about $17, which is an extremely small amount compared with the $80 I paid for a defective and unusable product.

I believe a full refund or a fair devolution is justified. I would have preferred to return the product to the seller rather than receive such an inadequate refund. The seller should cover the return shipping costs for this unusable product and provide me with a full refund of the amount I paid.

UPDATE after Aliexpress reply my opinion here: Despite providing extensive evidence directly to AliExpress, including videos, photos, and proof of the wig’s weight and condition, my appeals have been rejected more than three times. I also uploaded additional videos showing the uneven cuts and the actual weight of the wig on YouTube and X/Twitter.

The product I received was significantly different from what was advertised, and I believe the evidence clearly demonstrates this. It is very disappointing that, despite providing multiple forms of evidence, AliExpress continues to consider them insufficient. I was a frequent AliExpress buyer, so this experience has been extremely disappointing. I am sharing this update so other buyers can make an informed decision.

review_headline: Vedr. en retursag, hvor jeg ikke kan returnere ubrugelig vare.
review_body:

Jeg bad sælgeren, Podofo German Store om en retur adresse, samt email og et mobilnr.
Dette svarede han aldrig på, så jeg fandt en adr. på nettet i Frankfurt am Main, som jeg sendte pakken til, via UPS. 
Den blev nægtet modtaget og returneret til mig via UPS/Pakke.dk - det har koste mig 284,- kr. indtil videre plus selvfølgelig prisen på den uduelige Android unit, som kostede 143,16 euro = 1.080,- DKK.
Jeg har skrevet til sælgeren endnu engang og bedt om en korrekt returadresse, men han "spiller bare dum" og svarer ikke på det jeg beder om.

Når AliExpress sender mail til mig og skriver at de behandler sagen, på min email, kan man ikke besvare mailen fra dem. 
Sidste mail, med denne besked:
"We have conducted a thorough review regarding your request for this order. After careful consideration and verification, we regret to inform you that we are unable to proceed with a refund or compensation for this order.
We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this situation may cause and deeply appreciate your understanding and cooperation in this matter."

Det er så hvad man har ud af at handle med en platform, hvor sælgerne bare kan sende noget ubrugeligt bras og ikke vil modtage det retur.

review_headline: 172 Precio todo incluido.  191€ al ir a pagar. La magia de AliExpress
review_body:
Intenté comprar una mesa anunciada por 172,24 €. La oferta indicaba claramente: IVA incluido, envío gratuito, ahorro en aranceles y sin cargos sorpresa adicionales en la entrega. Todo parecía perfectamente claro… hasta que llegó el momento de pagar.

Al acceder al checkout, el mismo producto, la misma variante, una sola unidad y la misma dirección de entrega pasaron mágicamente a costar 191,38 €. Aparecieron 19,14 € adicionales sin identificar, justificar ni desglosar.

Contacté con Atención al Cliente `por chat, envié las capturas y expliqué detalladamente lo sucedido. El propio agente revisó las pruebas, reconoció que se trataba de “un defecto del sistema” y escaló el caso para que pudieran arreglarlo.

¿La solución final de AliExpress? Una respuesta aparentemente automatizada indicándome que comprobara el carrito, que los impuestos podían recalcularse y que, si el precio no cumplía mis expectativas, buscara productos similares de otros vendedores.

La ironía es perfecta: AliExpress muestra un precio final, lo incrementa sin explicación al ir a pagar y su “solución” consiste en recomendar al cliente que compre otra cosa.

Un usuario necesita algo más que una respuesta automatizada. Una entidad como la suya debe ofrecer, además de respuestas absurdas como la facilitada, SOLUCIONES a los clientes.

Dispongo de una grabación completa de la pantalla que muestra todo el proceso, además de las capturas y la conversación en la que su propio agente reconoce el fallo. Por tanto, no se trata de una percepción ni de que el precio “no cumpla mis expectativas”: se trata de una diferencia objetiva entre el precio anunciado y el exigido en el checkout.

He solicitado que reabran el caso, expliquen y desglosen los 19,14 € añadidos y me permitan comprar el producto al precio anunciado, aplicando además el cupón disponible en ese momento.

Hasta que AliExpress ofrezca una solución real, mi experiencia puede resumirse así: un precio atractivo para llegar al checkout, un incremento inexplicable al pagar y un servicio de atención al cliente que responde sin analizar las pruebas.

Señores de AliExpress!!, dejen de hacer magia y nos tomen a los consumidores por tontos!!!

review_headline: Une plateforme qui devient un parcours du combattant dès qu’un produit tombe en panne
review_body:
Achat effectué en décembre 2025, matériel reçu le 7 juin 2026, moteur HS dès le 8 juin. Depuis, je tente sans succès d’obtenir une résolution amiable.

J’ai pourtant fourni tout ce qui pouvait l’être : environ 28 photographies, photos de la machine, de l’emballage et du moteur, vidéo montrant le dysfonctionnement, explications détaillées, échanges avec le vendeur et réponses aux e-mails d’AliExpress. La même vidéo a été transmise plusieurs fois.

Malgré cela, le service client me réclame régulièrement exactement les mêmes photos et la même vidéo, comme si le dossier repartait systématiquement de zéro. Conversations interrompues, nouveaux agents, nouvelles demandes, nouvelles explications, nouvelles escalades… puis retour au point de départ.

Je conserve l’ensemble des échanges et des preuves. Je ne suis évidemment pas responsable de la mauvaise conservation ou du mauvais suivi des pièces transmises par AliExpress.

Le plus aberrant est que le vendeur lui-même avait reconnu le problème et proposé l’envoi d’un moteur de remplacement. Cette solution impliquait toutefois 17,30 € de frais de livraison à ma charge, ce que j’ai refusé pour un produit tombé en panne dès le lendemain de sa réception.

AliExpress a malgré tout refusé de résoudre le problème. Trois escalades successives ont été effectuées auprès de leurs services supérieurs sans résultat concret.

Puis on m’a indiqué que mon dossier était clôturé parce que le délai pour agir aurait été dépassé, alors que ce sont précisément les multiples demandes de preuves, échanges et escalades d’AliExpress qui ont fait durer la procédure. Faire traîner un dossier puis reprocher au client le temps écoulé est particulièrement difficile à comprendre.

Et maintenant, nouvelle absurdité : on me demande des preuves concernant un écran tactile et un écran LCD.

Problème : la machine que j’ai reçue ne possède ni écran tactile ni écran LCD. Elle possède un affichage numérique à LED rouges et des commandes physiques.

Je ne peux donc pas fournir une vidéo démontrant une fonctionnalité qui n’existe pas sur le matériel reçu.

Si AliExpress considère que le produit concerné doit posséder un écran tactile et un écran LCD, alors pourquoi m’a-t-on livré un produit qui n’en possède aucun ?

On m’a également indiqué que certaines photographies fournies ne correspondaient pas à l’article acheté, alors que je signale justement cette incohérence concernant le matériel reçu.

Même l’application AliExpress a présenté des dysfonctionnements pendant la procédure : étapes affichées sans éléments interactifs, procédure disparaissant après avoir quitté et rouvert l’application, historique ne reflétant pas l’ensemble de mes démarches.

Et pendant tout ce temps, le problème initial n’a jamais changé :

le moteur est HS depuis le 8 juin 2026.

J’ai été patient, coopératif et j’ai moi-même recherché une résolution amiable pendant des mois. Je n’ai jamais refusé de fournir les éléments disponibles. En revanche, je ne peux pas inventer un écran tactile inexistant ni fournir des preuves concernant un écran LCD absent du produit reçu.

Le problème n’est donc plus simplement un produit défectueux : c’est l’incapacité du service après-vente à traiter correctement un dossier pourtant documenté.

Le client doit continuellement prouver qu’il a déjà prouvé.

Et après tout cela, la réponse publique d’AliExpress à mon avis Trustpilot consiste simplement à m’indiquer qu’un e-mail m’a été envoyé et que je dois le consulter.

Cette réponse ne répond à rien : ni à la panne, ni aux preuves transmises, ni aux demandes répétitives, ni aux incohérences concernant le produit, ni aux frais de livraison, ni à la clôture du dossier, ni aux mois de démarches.

Une réponse générique n’est pas une résolution.

Au 28 août 2026, soit plus de deux mois et demi après la panne, le moteur est toujours HS et aucune solution sérieuse n’a été apportée.

J’ai désormais conservé l’intégralité du dossier et je vais transmettre les éléments aux organismes compétents afin que cette affaire soit examinée en dehors du système AliExpress.

review_headline: Mes 2 premières commandes par AliExpress du groupe Alibabasur…
review_body:
Mes 2 premières commandes sur AliExpress, qui dépend du groupe chinois Alibaba, l’équivalent d’Amazon, ont conduit aux faits suivants :
1er produit, un disque dur externe de 1 TO : Le 1er disque dur envoyé buggait aux transferts de gros fichiers. Là, pas de problème, je peux renvoyer le disque dur défaillant, je suis remboursé et je recommande un autre disque dur d’une marque célèbre, TOSHIBA : plus de problème.
2ième produit, N° de référence: 3072425932562583, un ordinateur portable vendu par un commerçant français. Cet achat est destiné à changer mon ordinateur portable HP dont certaines touches commencent à être illisibles et avec un message de défaillance de la batterie. Lorsque j’ai du temps je décide de changer d’ordinateur. A l’ouverture de l’ordinateur reçu d’AliExpress je constate que c’est un clavier « qwerty » et non pas « azerty », donc gros problème pour moi dont mon usage d’un ordinateur portable est pour l’écriture car sur un clavier « qwerty » les lettres sont disposées autrement, mais surtout, il n’y a pas les accents sur les a, les e et les u, comme il n’y a pas le ç. J’explique dès mon 1er courriel du 9 mai le problème à AliExpress avec photographies des 2 claviers. Réponse d’AliEXpress : « Nous vous prions de bien vouloir fournir une preuve valide, sous forme de vidéo, démontrant que le produit reçu ne fonctionne pas correctement, et ce dans un délai de 24 heures. ». Je réponds que ce n’est pas un problème de fonctionneement (software) mais un problème de type de clavier. Et depuis les échanges s’enchaînent ; AliExpress reste sur le fonctionnement de l’ordinateur, et moi sur le problème matériel du clavier, fournissant des photographies et explications plus précises, y compris le rappel à la loi française, c’est-à-dire aux articles L217-4 à L217-7 du Code de la consommation. Et in fine, hier, je les informe que je vais leur faire de la publicité gratuite. Il faut enfin ajouter ce fait, le coût de ce produit : 303,92 €.

review_headline: I bought an item worth over €240 that…
review_body:
I bought an item worth over €240 that explicitly guaranteed "Free Returns within 15 days" on the product page prior to my purchase.
When the package arrived, I received a completely different item from what was described. The error is 100% on their side. Yet, when I opened a return dispute, they completely refused to provide a free return label! They are now forcing me to pay heavy shipping fees out of my own pocket just to send back an item I never ordered in the first place.
Their customer support is useless, passing me around from one agent to another with zero results. This is deceptive advertising and a total trap for buyers. Do NOT buy from AliExpress—they do not respect their own return guarantees and will leave you stranded when they make a mistake!
The service was really bad, they do what they want, I recommend everyone look for an alternative on other sites.

Waardeloze garantie bij AliExpress: nul bescherming zodra een verkoper verdwijnt
​Koop op dit platform geen kostbare elektronica met de gedachte dat je garantie hebt. Ik heb een Junsun autoradio gekocht met een fabrieksgarantie van 2 jaar. Binnen deze garantietermijn begaf het apparaat het volledig. Om aan te tonen dat de inbouw en voeding in de auto 100% in orde waren, heb ik op eigen kosten een officieel rapport laten opstellen door een RDW-erkend autobedrijf. De diagnose was hard: een interne elektronische storing op de hoofdprintplaat van de radio.
​In de tussentijd is de winkel van de verkoper op AliExpress gesloten. Op dat moment zou de klantenservice van AliExpress het moeten overnemen en de garantie moeten waarborgen. De praktijk blijkt echter schrijnend:
​AliExpress biedt voor een product dat 100% defect is slechts een lachwekkende vergoeding van 30% aan.
​Nadat ik dit voorstel weigerde en verzocht om garantie (reparatie, vervanging, een volledige refund of store credit), weigert de klantenservice elke verdere medewerking omdat ik "het eerste bod heb afgewezen".
​Het platform neemt geen enkele verantwoordelijkheid voor verkopers die verdwijnen, terwijl ze wel commissie vangen over de verkopen.
​Kopersbescherming en 2 jaar garantie zijn bij AliExpress een lege belofte. Zodra een winkel de deuren sluit, verschuilt de klantenservice zich achter geautomatiseerde protocollen en laten ze de consument met een kapot product zitten. Wees gewaarschuwd!

review_headline: Aliexpress needs to vet their vendors…
review_body: Aliexpress needs to vet their vendors better, if they do at all. I ordered from four sellers. One sent the item. One used counterfeit postage and the post office would not deliver. One used a fake tracking number. And one just never sent the item. To the credit of Aliexpress they did get involved and refunded the three items I never got promptly. The sellers either never responded or ignored the issues. The one with the fake postage even wanted me to order more things to "make things right". No thanks! That was my one and only experience with Aliexpress, I will not try them again. So my beef is with the terrible scammers they allow on their site, as in the end Aliexpress did come through and refund everything I ordered and never recieved.

review_headline: Very Poor Return and Dispute Resolution Experience
review_body:
purchased a bicycle battery and received an item that did not match the description. In practice, I received a product that is unusable for me.
When I contacted the seller, they avoided taking responsibility and did not provide a clear solution. I then escalated the issue through AliExpress.
The decision was that I should return the item, and the seller would refund both the cost of the product and the shipping expenses. However, the shipping costs had to be agreed upon in advance.
The problem is that in my country, batteries cannot be sent by regular post because they fall under the category of dangerous goods. I tried to agree with the seller on the costs of using private shipping companies, but the seller kept avoiding a direct answer as to whether they would cover those costs or not.
As a result, the time allocated for resolving the dispute expired, and AliExpress closed the case.
After that, I contacted customer support seven times, and every time the result was the same: an AI-generated email that completely ignored the problems described during the conversation.
My advice: use PayPal when paying for purchases on AliExpress. I have heard that PayPal handles such return cases in the customer’s favour much more quickly and easily.
To sum up, if a problem arises, you receive AI-based support that appears to be poorly trained, and in reality, you become trapped in a pointless exchange of messages. It seems designed to make you give up and forget about the platform.

They trap buyers with glitched bots and keep money for defective garbage. Avoid buying electronics here!

Extremely disappointing experience with AliExpress and its customer service.

Order 3074763084437121. I returned a blue top that I had purchased through AliExpress, and the InPost tracking (820002887620010014839181) confirms that the parcel was shipped and received by the recipient.

AliExpress initially refused the refund and then claimed that “the item returned is different”, but has provided no clear evidence or explanation of what supposedly differs. The customer service is completely incapable of properly addressing the issue: instead of providing evidence or a concrete explanation, they simply repeat generic statements and close the appeal.

I have screenshots of the original order and of the item shown in my AliExpress app, as well as confirmation from InPost that the returned parcel was received. The original product page is no longer available.

At this point, I have neither the €105.69 I paid nor the returned item. This is an unacceptable way to handle a customer dispute. I have already escalated the matter through my bank and will take the matter further with the relevant authorities.

Very poor customer service and absolutely no meaningful explanation or resolution.

UPDATE 
After I posted my review, AliExpress finally sent me photos of what they claim was received. The item shown in the photos is a pair of shorts, not the blue top I returned.

Even more importantly, the photos show my name on the shipping label, but the packaging itself is NOT the package I sent. I returned the item in an H&M package. The package shown in AliExpress’ evidence is completely different.

I do not have a packing video because several weeks have passed since I returned the item, but I have witnesses who saw me put the correct item into the package and shipping it. The parcel was shipped on 1 August and, according to InPost tracking (820002887620010014839181), delivered on 14 August. (By the way, all this time??? And no one asks questions?? It should’ve been a couple of days, not weeks).

What is absolutely unacceptable is that AliExpress shows me evidence of a completely different package and item, yet does not seem interested at all in asking the courier what happened. If my label was attached to a different package, then obviously something happened during the return process — and somewhere there may be another customer who did not receive their own package either.

I did not choose the courier myself; the return shipping method was provided by AliExpress. Yet I am now expected to bear the entire financial loss for a problem that occurred after I handed the correct return to the courier.

I have already contacted InPost myself and requested an investigation, while AliExpress continues to focus only on the fact that I do not have a packing video instead of investigating the obvious discrepancy in the shipment.

I have neither my €105.69 nor the item I returned.

This is absolutely unacceptable and frankly disgraceful customer service. I expect AliExpress to investigate what happened to my parcel with the courier instead of simply refusing my refund.

review_headline: DEFECTIVE ITEM - NOT SUPPORTIVE NOT HELPFUL
review_body:
## ⭐ Buyer Protection That Doesn't Protect

I wanted to trust AliExpress, but my recent experience has completely changed my opinion.

## 📦 Damaged Items on Arrival

I received:

* **Solar eclipse glasses** with the filter lens folded and creased (a serious safety concern).
* **A vinyl car sticker** that was bent and wrinkled because it wasn't shipped flat.

Both items were clearly damaged during shipping due to poor packaging.

## 📷 I Provided Plenty of Evidence

I submitted:

* Multiple clear photos
* Close-up images
* Different angles
* Additional evidence every time it was requested

Despite this, AliExpress kept responding that my evidence was "not sufficient" and asked for even more.

## 🤷 Endless Requests, No Resolution

It felt like the goal wasn't to investigate the issue—it was simply to keep asking for more evidence until the buyer gave up.

When an item is obviously defective, buyers shouldn't have to repeatedly prove the same thing.

## ❌ Buyer Protection Felt Meaningless

The buyer protection policy sounds reassuring, but in my experience it didn't provide any real protection.

If damaged items with clear photographic evidence still don't qualify for a straightforward refund, I have to question how effective the dispute system really is.

## ⚠️ My Advice

Be cautious when buying from AliExpress.

If something arrives damaged, don't assume the buyer protection policy will work as advertised. My experience has left me with very little confidence in the platform, and I will think twice before ordering from them again.

review_body:
​Title:Deceptive Checkout System & Predatory Shipping Charges — Case Ref:3075642513206header
​AliExpress and the seller "Gather Here Store" are engaging in predatory & deceptive sales practices.
​I attempted to purchase 3 small wooden stamps from the same store in a single transaction. However, their broken system enforced an arbitrary purchasing limit of "1 unit per order", physically forcing me to split my purchase into multiple separate transactions. As a direct result, I was charged duplicate shipping fees (£2.66 each time)—a complete rip-off engineered by a system flaw.
​To make matters worse, the listings repeatedly claim "only 1 left in stock" to induce panic buying, yet the stock magically replenishes immediately after payment.
​When I raised this with customer service, an agent named Umar falsely assured me before checkout that the issue was resolved. It was not. The so-called "higher-level escalation" resulted in nothing more than a generic, copy-pasted email ignoring the actual technical glitch & refusing to refund the overcharged delivery fees.
​I have paid over £41 for these items—a subtotal that easily exceeds their £28 free-shipping threshold—yet I was scammed into paying duplicate shipping due to their system's refusal to combine orders.
​I demand an immediate refund of the £5.32 overcharged shipping fee and an investigation into this fake scarcity tactic. I have full screenshot evidence of every chat log, system error, and invoice, and I will report this to the UK Financial Ombudsman and Consumer Rights authorities if left unresolved.

Title: A £300 Deceptive Trap - How AliExpress Exploits "Fairness" for Profit
​Review:
I am writing this to expose how AliExpress and its sellers (specifically Gather Here Store) manipulate the system to exploit buyers. I attempted to purchase a 15-piece wooden stamp set. Individually, these items are priced around £20 each. For a full set, this represents a significant investment of approximately £300.
​The "Fairness" Scam:
The seller intentionally broke the 15-piece set into 15 separate listings. AliExpress then imposed a strict limit of "1 item per order." To acquire the full set, I was forced to place 15 separate orders. Because they split the listings, I was forced to pay £2.66 in shipping for every single item—totalling nearly £40 in unnecessary shipping fees.
​When I challenged this, AliExpress customer support claimed these limits were set by the seller to ensure "fair buying opportunities for everyone" during a promotion. This is a blatant, insulting lie:
​They are selling wooden stamps, not scarce medical supplies or emergency goods. There is zero logical reason to enforce "anti-hoarding" rules on stationery.
​The system allows me to buy all 15 pieces, but only if I pay the seller 15 separate shipping fees. Where is the "fairness" in paying 15x the shipping cost for a single transaction?
​This is purely a deceptive tactic to bypass "Free Shipping" thresholds and extract hidden profits from customers.
​AliExpress support has proven useless, repeatedly stalling with requests for "supplementary documents" every 48 hours to delay resolution. They essentially told me to negotiate shipping fees directly with the seller. If I have to deal with the seller directly to resolve platform traps, then the AliExpress platform serves no purpose other than to facilitate these scams.
​Be warned: This platform is not a marketplace; it is a trap designed to extract extra fees through absurd, artificial restrictions. Do not trust their "promotions" or "fairness" claims.

​I purchased a fitness tracker (Order #1118274496035281) which worked fine for six months before completely dying overnight. It won’t charge, it won’t turn on, and it’s completely unresponsive. The seller confirmed in writing that the product has a one-year warranty.

After finally reaching a human support agent, their response was infuriatingly absurd: they claimed that the video I provided “failed to detect the defect of the equipment” and demanded a video showing the “obvious defects when you use the equipment.”
​How on earth are you supposed to "use" a device that is completely dead and won't charge?! What do they expect? A magic show?
​This is a deliberate, transparent tactic to exhaust customers and cheat them out of valid warranty claims. They hide behind impossible demands ("official inspection reports" or videos of a dead brick performing functions) so they never have to honor a single refund or replacement.
​AliExpress Customer Care does not care about consumers. Save your money, buy from reputable local retailers, and avoid getting scammed by their fake "warranties."

⭐ 1 Stern – Sehr enttäuschende Erfahrung mit dem Kundenservice

Ich habe bei AliExpress Echthaar für über 200 € bestellt. Leider entsprach die Qualität nach kurzer Zeit nicht mehr meinen Erwartungen: Das Haar wurde stumpf, verfilzte bzw. verhedderte sich, die Dichte nahm in den Längen deutlich ab und die Enden waren teilweise extrem dünn und wirkten abgebrochen.

Ich habe zunächst versucht, das Problem direkt mit dem Verkäufer zu lösen. Der Verkäufer machte mir im Laufe der Kommunikation mehrere unterschiedliche Angebote zur Rückerstattung. Ich war sogar bereit, dem Verkäufer noch eine weitere Chance zu geben und erneut bei ihm zu bestellen, da ich davon ausgehe, dass möglicherweise eine schlechte Charge die Ursache gewesen sein könnte.

Da wir keine endgültige Lösung fanden, wandte ich mich an den AliExpress-Kundenservice.

AliExpress forderte ausdrücklich Video-/Bildbeweise. Ich habe daraufhin ZWEI Videos eingereicht, in denen das Haar selbst der klare Fokus ist. Das Haar wurde aus mehreren Perspektiven, aus der Nähe und in verschiedenen Bereichen gezeigt, damit die Qualität, die Struktur, die Dichte und insbesondere die sehr dünnen und beschädigten wirkenden Enden deutlich erkennbar sind.

Zunächst wurde mir mitgeteilt, es seien keine Beweise vorgelegt worden. Nachdem ich darauf hingewiesen hatte, dass ich zwei Videos eingereicht habe, änderte sich die Begründung: Nun hieß es, die Beweise seien zwar vorhanden, würden aber nicht ausreichen. Eine konkrete Erklärung, welcher Teil der Videos nicht erkennbar sein soll, erhielt ich nicht.

Anschließend wurde plötzlich ein Qualitätsbericht eines Drittanbieters verlangt.

Ich habe mehrfach ausführlich erklärt, dass es sich um einen sichtbaren Qualitätsmangel des Produktes handelt und dass das Produkt selbst in den Videos eindeutig zu sehen ist. Trotzdem erhielt ich wiederholt nahezu wortgleiche Standardantworten.

Was mich besonders enttäuscht, ist nicht nur die Ablehnung meiner Rückerstattung, sondern dass ich das Gefühl hatte, dass meine konkreten Beweise und meine ausführliche Erklärung überhaupt nicht individuell geprüft wurden. Ich habe immer wieder dieselben Antworten erhalten, ohne eine konkrete Auseinandersetzung mit meinen Videos oder dem Chatverlauf mit dem Verkäufer.

Bei einem Warenwert von über 200 € hätte ich eine ernsthafte und nachvollziehbare Prüfung erwartet.

Ich habe dem Verkäufer und auch AliExpress mehrfach die Möglichkeit gegeben, eine faire Lösung zu finden. Leider hatte ich am Ende den Eindruck, dass so lange Standardantworten wiederholt wurden, bis der Kunde irgendwann aufgibt.

Für mich ist das eine sehr enttäuschende Erfahrung. Nicht wegen einer einzelnen schlechten Lieferung, sondern vor allem wegen des Umgangs mit meiner Reklamation und der fehlenden nachvollziehbaren Begründung für die Ablehnung.

Ich kann aufgrund dieser Erfahrung aktuell leider keine positive Empfehlung für den AliExpress-Kundenservice aussprechen.

review_headline: AliExpress account stuck in an endless…
review_body:
AliExpress account stuck in an endless authentication loop for over two months. Password reset works for three days, then the system forces another reset. On iPhone I cannot log in at all.
Case ID: 2053808358289979
Dozens of support tickets, only automated replies. No human has reviewed this case. Requesting escalation to a technical engineer.

UPDATE 19/08: I regained access on 18/08 via password reset on desktop, and password is currently the only working sign-in method. During testing, password, email code, passkey and Google all led to a forced "Change password" screen. Passkey authentication completed successfully but then returned "Account disabled", and the "Enable Now" button on that screen links to survey.aliexpress.com — a closed page. There is no working self-service recovery path. The recovery URL contained identityScene=RELEASE_STOLEN, which suggests a security flag remains on the account.

UPDATE 23/08: Still no response since my reply of 19 August, and the 7–14 business day window AliExpress stated has now passed. Desktop sign-in with password has been stable for two weeks, but passkey sign-in still returns "Account disabled" and the "Enable Now" button still redirects to a closed survey page. I have not reinstalled the app on my iPhone, because every previous attempt triggered an "unusual activity" lock that also broke my working desktop session — and AliExpress has not answered my request for guidance on how to safely sign in from that device. On 19/08 AliExpress invited me to reply to their agent directly. When I did, the same mailbox returned an automated message stating that emails sent to it are not received. There is now no working channel through which this case can be reached.

UPDATE 26/08 — FINAL: Desktop access has now been lost as well. After two weeks of stable sign-in, I am locked out of every device. Three months, dozens of tickets, and this is where it ends.

The record speaks for itself. AliExpress told me the problem was fixed — it was not, and I proved it with screenshots the same day. They asked me questions, I answered in full, and they never replied. They invited me to write to their agent directly, and that same mailbox now auto-replies that emails to it are not received. Their own "Enable Now" recovery button leads to a dead survey page. There is not one working channel left through which a customer can reach a human being about a broken account.

This is not a technical failure. A technical failure gets fixed. This is a company that has decided that individual customers are not worth answering — that a buyer of many years can be locked out of his own account for three months, document everything, follow every instruction given to him, and simply be ignored until he gives up. That is the actual policy, whatever the support templates say.

To anyone reading this before you buy: the products may be cheap, but if anything goes wrong with your account there is no one behind the counter. Not a person, not a phone number, not a working email. You are entirely on your own.

I am done. Case ID: 2053808358289979 — unresolved, abandoned.
